raw_response:
I need to think carefully about this year. I've got 9.5 mu, split between 4.5 mu of wheat-maize double crop and 5 mu of cotton. It's just me and my husband now — our children are working in Shijiazhuang — and he takes construction jobs in the county town whenever they call him. So I'm basically farming alone most days, and at 56, I have to be realistic about how much I can handle. I've been doing this for 30 years though, so I know what works on my fields.

The wheat went in last October, same as always. I used an improved variety, not the newest one but the one I've had good luck with. I put down base fertilizer then — about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's March and the wheat is greening up. The extension technician came by last month and said I should topdress at jointing, about 20 kg of urea per mu. I'll do that. Urea is expensive this year, over 2.5 yuan per kg, but I can't skip it — if the wheat turns yellow, I'll lose too much. I'll irrigate right after fertilizing to wash it in, and then probably once more at heading if it stays dry. That's three irrigations total including the winter one. I don't plan much pesticide for wheat, maybe one fungicide spray if I see rust. I should get around 400 kg/mu if the weather holds. Last year was 420, but I'm being cautious.

For cotton, I'll plant in late April. Cotton is our main cash crop but it's heavy on labor. I buy improved seed every year — saved seed doesn't work well for cotton. I'll plow and harrow the 5 mu in April, spread about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and plant. At flowering I'll topdress with another 15 kg of urea per mu. Cotton needs water at the right times — I'll irrigate twice, at flowering and boll setting. The pumping costs about 40 yuan each time per mu, so I won't overdo it. But pests are the real problem. I'll spray herbicide before planting, and then insecticide at least three times for bollworm and aphids. The chemicals add up to over 100 yuan per mu. I have to hire help for cotton — about two days per mu for planting and picking, because I can't manage 5 mu alone before the bolls spoil. I expect about 220 kg/mu of lint cotton.

After wheat harvest in mid-June, there's almost no time before maize planting. We'll get a custom harvester for the wheat — it's 50 yuan per mu but worth it for the speed. Then quick rotary tillage and plant the maize. I use hybrid seed, about 25 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 25 kg per mu, and if the maize looks yellow at the big flare stage, I'll topdress urea. Summer maize usually gets some rain, so I'll only irrigate once unless July is very dry. One herbicide spray should be enough. Maize is the easiest crop for us — me and my husband can manage it without hired help, and I expect 450 kg/mu.

Adding everything up — seed, fertilizer, pesticides, irrigation electricity, and hired labor for cotton — I'll spend about 4,300 yuan this year. That's a lot for us. My husband's off-farm work brings in some cash, but we need to keep money aside for medicine and emergencies. So I'm not maxing out inputs. I'm doing what I know works, what I can afford, and what my labor can handle. Better steady than sorry.
